## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
When typing an emoji shortcode in the composer (e.g., `:sta` or `:star`), suggestions appear for emojis whose names do not contain the typed prefix (e.g., `:moyai:` or `:dizzy:`), showing no highlighted text or context for why they were matched.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
1. In `src/libs/EmojiTrie.ts:115-117`, `addKeywordsToTrie` indexes English and localized keywords into the Trie (e.g., `statue` -> `:moyai:`, `star` -> `:dizzy:`).
2. In `src/libs/EmojiUtils.tsx:suggestEmojis`, `trie.getAllMatchingWords` collects emojis matching by name, alias, or keyword prefix.
3. While `sortByName` (`EmojiUtils.tsx:111-123`) sorts name matches ahead of keyword matches, `EmojiSuggestionItem.tsx` only renders `item.name` and highlights matches against `item.name` (`getStyledTextArray(item.name, prefix)`). Because the matched keyword is omitted from the UI, keyword-only matches appear completely disconnected and unhighlighted to the user.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. In `src/libs/EmojiUtils.tsx:suggestEmojis`, attach the triggering keyword to suggestion items when matched via keyword nodes in the Trie (e.g., `matchedKeyword: node.name`).
2. In `src/components/EmojiSuggestions/EmojiSuggestionItem.tsx`, when an emoji is matched via a keyword rather than its name/alias, display the matched keyword next to the emoji name (e.g. `:dizzy: (star)`), highlighting the prefix within the keyword.
3. If product prefers restricting composer inline shortcodes to names and aliases only, add a parameter to `suggestEmojis` to skip keyword nodes during inline autocomplete.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
When typing an emoji shortcode in the composer (such as `:star`), the autocomplete suggestions menu displays irrelevant emojis whose names do not contain the typed prefix (e.g., `:moyai:` or `:dizzy:`), showing no highlighted text or context for why they were matched.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
1. In `src/libs/EmojiTrie.ts:115-125`, `addKeywordsToTrie` indexes keywords into the Trie (e.g. `statue` -> `:moyai:`, `star` -> `:dizzy:`, `stars and stripes` -> `:us:`).
2. In `src/libs/EmojiUtils.tsx:suggestEmojis`, `trie.getAllMatchingWords` collects all matching Trie nodes (both emoji names and keyword nodes) up to `limit`. Because keyword-matching nodes and emoji name nodes share the same trie prefix search, keyword-only matches occupy suggestion slots before other genuine name-matching emojis deeper in the trie can be gathered.
3. In `src/components/EmojiSuggestions/EmojiSuggestionItem.tsx`, the row only renders `item.name` and highlights the typed prefix using `getStyledTextArray(item.name, prefix)`. Because keyword-only matches have no string overlap with `item.name`, they render with zero highlighted characters, appearing completely disconnected and broken to the user.
4. Additionally, in `suggestEmojis`, `if (!suggestions) return;` erroneously exits the entire function early instead of continuing to the next matching node.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. In `src/libs/EmojiUtils.tsx:suggestEmojis`:
   - Prioritize name and alias prefix matches first so direct prefix matches fill the suggestion slots up to `limit`.
   - When matching via keyword nodes, only add keyword suggestions if `matching.length < limit`, and pass the matched keyword along with the item (or restrict inline colon autocomplete to name/alias matches only, which aligns with standard shortcode autocomplete).
   - Fix line 590: change `if (!suggestions) return;` to `if (!suggestions) continue;` so an empty node doesn't abort iterating subsequent valid matches.
2. In `src/components/EmojiSuggestions/EmojiSuggestionItem.tsx`:
   - If keyword matches are retained in inline autocomplete, display the matched keyword tag next to the name (e.g., `:dizzy: (star)`) with the matching characters highlighted so the user sees why the emoji was suggested.

### What alternative solutions did you explore?
Filter suggestions in `suggestEmojis` for inline composer autocomplete so that only emojis whose `name` or `aliases` contain the typed prefix are returned (matching standard Slack/Discord shortcode behavior), while preserving full keyword search in the standalone Emoji Picker.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

[Add liquid glass bottom tab bar to iOS, Android and mWeb](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/101339) (`Expensify/App#101339`) introduced this regression. It merged on 2026-10-15, so it is on staging but not on production.

The native tab bar has room for five of the six tabs. The Insights beta decides which tab gets no bar item. With the beta on, Account loses its item. With the beta off, Insights loses it ([getTabWithoutBarItem.ts:8-10](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4c2dc1d0ba855aa5dee6a7a7c26ac620a622dc3b/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/NativeTabNavigator/getTabWithoutBarItem.ts#L8-L10), [TabNavigator.native.tsx:41-48](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4c2dc1d0ba855aa5dee6a7a7c26ac620a622dc3b/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx#L41-L48)).

The hidden-tab patch gives a hidden tab no native screen ([hidden-tab-items.patch:68-69](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4c2dc1d0ba855aa5dee6a7a7c26ac620a622dc3b/patches/react-navigation/%40react-navigation%2Bbottom-tabs%2B7.19.2%2B003%2Bhidden-tab-items.patch#L68-L69)). So toggling the beta removes one native tab view and adds another inside the same native tab host. The host keeps the same fixed key, `"native-tabs-host"` ([patch:95](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4c2dc1d0ba855aa5dee6a7a7c26ac620a622dc3b/patches/react-navigation/%40react-navigation%2Bbottom-tabs%2B7.19.2%2B003%2Bhidden-tab-items.patch#L95)).

On Android, react-native-screens' `TabsContainer` does not clear its selected tab key when that tab's view is removed. The Account tab is selected while you toggle the beta in Beta overrides. When you disable the beta, Account's native screen comes back, but the native host still points at the old one. Native updates wait until the host is shown again. When you tap back, the host reattaches, restores state from the stale key, and an RNScreens check throws. The app crashes.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Remount the native tab host when the tab without a bar item changes, so RNScreens starts from a clean state:

- In the hidden-tab patch, include the hidden route keys in the `Tabs.Host` key instead of the fixed `"native-tabs-host"`.
- Simpler option: add `key={tabWithoutBarItem}` to `<Tab.Navigator>` in [TabNavigator.native.tsx:51](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/4c2dc1d0ba855aa5dee6a7a7c26ac620a622dc3b/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx#L51).

Each beta flip then remounts the tab screens once. Beta flips are rare, so this cost is fine. Test on a device that the user stays on the Account tab after the remount.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- Patch RNScreens `TabsContainer` on Android. When the selected tab's view is removed, it should drop that fragment and reset its navigation state. This fixes the root cause, but the change is larger and is in native code. It is worth raising upstream.
- Changing JS navigation state (for example, `useIsSettingsDrawnOverTabs` or the Insights redirect) will not help. The bad state is inside the native host.

<details>
<summary>Investigation details and confidence</summary>

**Confidence: medium.** The beta-driven native tab swap from the PR above is the only native change that depends on this beta, and the staging-only timing matches. I worked out the exact native code path and exception from the source code. I did not reproduce the crash on a device. An Android logcat or Sentry stack trace would confirm the exception. Likely messages are `[RNScreens] No selected tab present`, `Requested fragment for key ... does not exist`, and `Unexpected fragment manager state`.

**Why the crash happens on back, not on toggle:** Beta overrides opens in the RHP, which covers the tab navigator in the root native stack. `TabsContainer` applies pending updates only after the host is attached to the window again. Enabling the beta probably survives because the selection ends as a repeated selection. That leaves a stale Account fragment behind, and disabling the beta then hits it. I have not confirmed this on a device.

**Open question:** Whether iOS has the same problem. The report lists Android only.

</details>

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
On Android, after disabling "Insights Page" beta in Troubleshoot > Beta overrides, navigating back crashes the app.

2. In `hidden-tab-items.patch`, `NativeBottomTabView` wraps tabs in `<Tabs.Host key="native-tabs-host">`. The hidden route renders outside `Tabs.Host` in an absolute View.
3. Disabling the beta flips `tabWithoutBarItem` from Settings to Insights. Because `Tabs.Host` has a fixed key `"native-tabs-host"`, React mutates children in-place rather than remounting the container.
4. On Android, `react-native-screens`' `TabsHostViewManager` cannot re-index tabs dynamically without corrupting FragmentManager state (`TabsContainer` does not unmount replaced views in Fabric). Popping the RHP triggers an unhandled native crash.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
In `src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx:51`:

```typescript
    return (
        <Tab.Navigator
            key={tabWithoutBarItem}
            backBehavior="fullHistory"
            layout={renderNativeTabLayout}
```
Passing `key={tabWithoutBarItem}` remounts the native tab container cleanly when the beta changes, preventing in-place fragment mutation.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
On Android, after enabling and then disabling the "Insights Page" beta in `Troubleshoot > Beta overrides`, navigating back to the previous screen causes the application to crash.

---

### What is the root cause of that problem?

1. **Native Tab Bar Slot Limitation & Dynamic Slot Allocation:**
   In [PR #101339](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/101339) (*"Add liquid glass bottom tab bar to iOS, Android and mWeb"*), the native bottom tab bar was introduced. The native bar can accommodate up to 5 tabs:
   - When the `InsightsPage` beta is **enabled**: `SCREENS.INSIGHTS` is displayed in the native bar, and Account (`NAVIGATORS.SETTINGS_SPLIT_NAVIGATOR`) is hidden from the bar (`tabWithoutBarItem = NAVIGATORS.SETTINGS_SPLIT_NAVIGATOR`, as defined in `getTabWithoutBarItem.ts`).
   - When the `InsightsPage` beta is **disabled**: `NAVIGATORS.SETTINGS_SPLIT_NAVIGATOR` is displayed in the bar, and `SCREENS.INSIGHTS` has no bar item (`tabWithoutBarItem = SCREENS.INSIGHTS`).

2. **Static Key Collision in `hidden-tab-items.patch`:**
   In `patches/react-navigation/@react-navigation+bottom-tabs+7.19.2+003+hidden-tab-items.patch` (line 95), `NativeBottomTabView` wraps the active bar tabs in:
   ```tsx
   Tabs.Host({ key: "native-tabs-host", ... })
   ```
   Tabs marked with `tabBarItemHidden: true` are excluded from `Tabs.Host` and rendered outside in an absolute overlay `View`.

3. **Android `react-native-screens` Fragment Lifecycle Failure:**
   - When the user toggles the `InsightsPage` beta override off while inside `Beta overrides` (which is part of the Account/Settings split navigator), `tabWithoutBarItem` immediately switches from `SETTINGS_SPLIT_NAVIGATOR` to `INSIGHTS`.
   - Because `<Tabs.Host>` retains the fixed key `"native-tabs-host"`, React performs an **in-place reconciliation** of its children instead of unmounting and remounting the container.
   - On Android (Fabric), `react-native-screens`' `TabsHostViewManager` and `TabsContainer` manage native Android fragments corresponding to tab screens. `TabsContainer` does not support dynamically swapping and re-indexing child Fragment views in-place without destroying and recreating the container.
   - While the user is in `Beta overrides` (a modal in the RHP), the tab host is temporarily detached from the active window. Once the user taps the back button to dismiss the RHP, the tab host reattaches to the window. `TabsContainer` attempts to restore fragment state using the stale route key/index from the previous configuration, triggering an unhandled native exception (`[RNScreens] No selected tab present` / corrupted `FragmentManager` transaction), resulting in an immediate crash.
   - iOS does not crash because `UITabBarController` supports dynamic re-assignment of `viewControllers` in place.

---

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In `src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx`, pass `key={tabWithoutBarItem}` to `<Tab.Navigator>`:

```diff
diff --git a/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx b/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx
--- a/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx
+++ b/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/Navigators/TabNavigator.native.tsx
@@ -51,6 +51,7 @@ function TabNavigator() {
     return (
         <Tab.Navigator
+            key={tabWithoutBarItem}
             backBehavior="fullHistory"
             layout={renderNativeTabLayout}
             screenLayout={bottomTabScreenLayoutWrapper}
```

#### Why this solution is safe, robust, and preserves state:
1. **State Preservation:**
   `TabNavigator` already implements state persistence across unmounts/remounts via `usePreserveNavigatorState` in `useNativeTabNavigator.ts` (lines 110–121):
   ```ts
   const tabRouterOverride = (originalRouter) => ({
       getInitialState: (configOptions) => {
           const preserved = getPreservedNavigatorState(route.key);
           return preserved ? originalRouter.getRehydratedState(preserved, configOptions) : originalRouter.getInitialState(configOptions);
       },
   });
   ```
   Because `route.key` remains unchanged, when `Tab.Navigator` remounts with the new key, `tabRouterOverride` rehydrates the preserved navigation state cleanly. The user remains on the Account tab without losing their place or navigation history.
2. **Clean Native Lifecycle:**
   Remounting `Tab.Navigator` completely tears down the old `Tabs.Host` and initializes a fresh native `TabsContainer` with the new 5 tabs in their proper indices, completely eliminating the fragment collision on Android.
3. **No Overhead During Normal Usage:**
   `tabWithoutBarItem` only changes when the beta status is toggled (which only occurs inside `Beta overrides` or upon permissions update). It does not change during standard app navigation, so there is zero runtime penalty or unnecessary remounting during regular usage.

---

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

1. **Patching `hidden-tab-items.patch`:**
   Keying `Tabs.Host` dynamically inside `hidden-tab-items.patch` (e.g. `key={tabWithoutBarItem}`). 
   - *Downside:* Modifies third-party patch files (`patches/react-navigation/...`), increasing maintenance burden and complexity during future React Navigation version upgrades. A pure JS solution in `TabNavigator.native.tsx` is cleaner and easier to maintain.
2. **Patching `react-native-screens` Android native source:**
   Modifying `TabsContainer.kt` to handle dynamic child mutations gracefully.
   - *Downside:* Far more invasive, requires maintaining native Kotlin patches for `react-native-screens`, and does not provide any additional benefit over a clean container remount.

   ```ts
       },
   });
   ```
   Because `route.key` remains unchanged, when `Tab.Navigator` remounts with the new key, `tabRouterOverride` rehydrates the preserved navigation state cleanly. The user remains on the Account tab without losing their place, scroll position, or navigation history.
2. **Clean Native Lifecycle:**
   Remounting `Tab.Navigator` completely tears down the old native `TabsContainer` and initializes a fresh instance with the new 5 tabs in their proper indices, completely eliminating the fragment collision on Android.
3. **Zero Overhead During Normal Usage:**
   `tabWithoutBarItem` only changes when the beta status is toggled (which only occurs inside `Beta overrides` or upon permissions update). It does not change during standard app navigation, so there is zero runtime penalty or unnecessary remounting during regular usage.

---

### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests?

1. **Unit Test for `getTabWithoutBarItem` (`tests/unit/getTabWithoutBarItemTest.ts`):**
   - Verify that when `isInsightsBetaEnabled` is `true`, `getTabWithoutBarItem` returns `NAVIGATORS.SETTINGS_SPLIT_NAVIGATOR`.
   - Verify that when `isInsightsBetaEnabled` is `false`, `getTabWithoutBarItem` returns `SCREENS.INSIGHTS`.
2. **Navigation State Preservation Test (`tests/unit/TabNavigatorStatePreservationTest.ts`):**
   - Verify that when `TabNavigator` remounts with a new `tabWithoutBarItem` key, `tabRouterOverride` invokes `getPreservedNavigatorState` and preserves the active tab and nested route state.

---

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

1. **Patching `hidden-tab-items.patch`:**
   Keying `Tabs.Host` dynamically inside `hidden-tab-items.patch` (e.g. `key={tabWithoutBarItem}`). 
   - *Downside:* Modifies third-party patch files (`patches/react-navigation/...`), increasing maintenance burden and complexity during future React Navigation version upgrades. A pure JS solution in `TabNavigator.native.tsx` is cleaner and easier to maintain.
2. **Patching `react-native-screens` Android native source:**
   Modifying `TabsContainer.kt` to handle dynamic child mutations gracefully.
   - *Downside:* Far more invasive, requires maintaining native Kotlin patches for `react-native-screens`, and does not provide any additional benefit over a clean container remount.

## Proposal ### What is the root cause of that problem? [Add Contains / Equal to match type for the Merchant filter](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/83733) (merged 2026-10-14) introduced this regression. It added `merchant*:` as the syntax for a "Contains" match. - The parser reads a typed `merchant:coffee` as a "Contains" filter. It does not keep the `:` the user typed. - When the app turns the query back into text, it always writes "Contains" as `*:`. - When you submit, the router rewrites the query this way. When you reopen the router, it fills the input from the same rebuilt text. So `merchant:coffee` comes back as `merchant*:coffee`. I reproduced this on web: the reopened router shows `type:expense merchant*:coffee`.
Code references - The parser turns a positive `merchant:` into `contains`: [searchParser.peggy:246-249](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchParser/searchParser.peggy#L246-L249) - `contains` maps to `*:`: [SearchQueryUtils.ts:99](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts#L99) - `buildFilterValuesString` writes `merchant*:`. Every query-to-text path calls it: [SearchQueryUtils.ts:676-683](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts#L676-L683) - The filter UI builds `merchant*:` for Contains: [SearchQueryUtils.ts:154-158](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts#L154-L158) - The router rewrites the query on submit: [SearchRouter.tsx:399](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/Search/SearchRouter/SearchRouter.tsx#L399) - The router fills the input from `buildUserReadableQueryString` when it reopens: [SearchRouter.tsx:140-179](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/Search/SearchRouter/SearchRouter.tsx#L140-L179) Merchant is the only filter affected. `*:` on any other key falls back to a keyword search.
### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem? Write merchant "Contains" as `merchant:` instead of `merchant*:` when building query text. - In `buildFilterValuesString`, use `:` when the filter is merchant and the operator is `contains`. - In `buildMerchantFilterQuery`, use `:` for the Contains match type. - Keep `*:` in the grammar, so typed `merchant*:x` still works. It will be shown as `merchant:x`, which means the same thing. - Update the unit tests in `tests/unit/Search/SearchQueryUtilsTest.ts` that expect `merchant*:`. The round trip still works, because `merchant:` already parses as Contains and `merchant=` stays exact. The query you see then matches what you typed. Saved-search hashes for merchant queries also return to their values from before the PR. ### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional) Change only the display. Keep `merchant*:` as the stored form, and show `merchant:` only in `buildUserReadableQueryString`. This keeps the current hashes, but the URL would still show `merchant*:`. --- **Next Steps for Contributor+ team:** **To accept:** `@MelvinBot implement [this](#proposal)` to create a draft PR. **To refine:** `@MelvinBot ` **To reject:** Explain why you are rejecting Melvin's proposal. --- _[view run](https://github.com/Expensify/melvin/actions/runs/39053958088)_ · _[view recording](https://melvinbot-assets.exops.io/session-39053958088-1-63184fd4-90a1-49c9-b4ec-37143d245fbc.webm)_ Contributor details Your Expensify account email: camesenin@gmail.com Upwork Profile Link: https://www.upwork.com/freelancers/~01b60d704ba377be83 ## Proposal ### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue. When searching for an expense using the merchant filter (e.g., `merchant:coffee`), reopening or re-submitting the search query in the search bar automatically appends an asterisk (`*`) to the merchant filter, changing it to `merchant*:coffee`. ### What is the root cause of that problem? In `buildMerchantFilterQuery` (line 156), write the default positive `CONTAINS` operator as `:`: ```typescript if (!isNegated) { operator = selectedMerchantOperator === CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO ? EXPLICIT_EQUAL_TO_OPERATOR : operatorToCharMap[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO] : operatorToCharMap[queryFilter.operator]; ``` 3. Keep `*:` in `src/libs/SearchParser/searchParser.peggy` for backward compatibility so typed queries containing `*:` continue to parse as `contains`, while ensuring serialization always outputs the clean `merchant:` syntax. 4. Update unit test assertions in `tests/unit/Search/SearchQueryUtilsTest.ts`. ### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional) Display-only conversion in `buildUserReadableQueryString`: rejected because keeping `merchant*:` in the internal serialized query string would still leak the asterisk into the URL route and break saved search query hashes. - **Platform Verification:** - [x] Web (Chrome / Safari) - [x] Mobile Web (iOS / Android) - [x] Desktop (MacOS / Windows) ## Proposal ### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue. After searching `merchant:coffee`, reopening the search router shows `merchant*:coffee`. The query the user typed gets rewritten with an asterisk they never entered. ### What is the root cause of that problem? I agree with the regression source (#83733). I want to point out where the `*:` actually comes from, because it reaches more than the router text. 1. The parser keeps the legacy meaning of a positive `merchant:` by turning it into `contains` ([searchParser.peggy:246-249](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchParser/searchParser.peggy#L246-L249)). 2. Every place that turns a `contains` filter back into text reads one map, `operatorToCharMap`, and that map says `CONTAINS: '*:'` ([SearchQueryUtils.ts:97-100](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts#L97-L100)). It is used by `buildFilterValuesString` ([L676-683](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts#L676-L683)) and `buildMerchantFilterQuery` ([L154-157](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts#L154-L157)). 3. `buildFilterValuesString` isn't only used for display. `getQueryHashes` and `getQueryHashWithoutFilters` build the hash string with it too ([L946-1057](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts#L946-L1057)). So the asterisk also changed the hash of every existing `merchant:` query. That hash keys saved searches and search snapshots. You can see this in the test that guards hash stability. Before #83733, `buildSearchQueryJSON('type:expense merchant:Amazon').hash` was pinned to `1692688529` ([parent commit a4e971f, SearchQueryUtilsTest.ts:2739](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/a4e971f741f6338d3fb15d3c5258cdcf56e004ad/tests/unit/Search/SearchQueryUtilsTest.ts#L2739)). #83733 changed the expectation to `1712664595` and added the comment "`merchant:` parses as contains and hashes as `merchant*:`" ([SearchQueryUtilsTest.ts:2948-2954](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/tests/unit/Search/SearchQueryUtilsTest.ts#L2948-L2954)). I rebuilt the hash input with the same `hashCode` function. The two values come from `type:expense status: groupBy:undefined merchant:Amazon sortBy:date sortOrder:desc columns:undefined`, with and without the `*`. So the extra `*` is the only reason the hash changed. ### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem? Fix it where the `*:` comes from, in `operatorToCharMap`, instead of adding merchant special cases at each place that writes the query: ```diff const operatorToCharMap = { [CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO]: ':' as const, - [CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.CONTAINS]: '*:' as const, + // A positive `merchant:` already parses as contains (`merchant=` is the exact match), so write contains as `:`. + // `*:` stays accepted by the parser for queries and URLs saved since #83733. + [CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.CONTAINS]: ':' as const, ``` Why this is safe: - Only merchant can hold `contains` in a parsed query. The parser turns `contains` on any other key, or a negated one, into a keyword ([peggy:219-222, 251-254](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/SearchParser/searchParser.peggy#L251-L254)). Description's `eq` to `contains` swap happens only in `serializeQueryJSONForBackend`, which never writes text. So the change can't alter any other filter. - Exact match still writes `=`, through the `EXPLICIT_EQUAL_TO_OPERATOR` branch, so `merchant=` and `merchant:` still round-trip as two different filters. - Both branches of `buildMerchantFilterQuery` (the new-clause one at L154-157 and the clause-rewrite one that calls `buildFilterValuesString`) pick up `:` automatically. The router text, URL `q`, pills, hashes, and the Merchant filter form all agree with no extra branches. - The `*:` token stays in the grammar. Links, recent searches, and saved-search queries written as `merchant*:x` between 10/14 and the fix still parse as contains, and they show up as `merchant:x`. - Hashes for `merchant:` queries go back to their pre-#83733 values. That is exactly what the hash-stability test is meant to guarantee, because these hashes key saved searches and snapshots. Then update the `merchant*:` output expectations in `tests/unit/Search/SearchQueryUtilsTest.ts` to `merchant:`. Inputs that use `merchant*:` stay as they are, because they still parse. ### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests? - Restore `expect(buildSearchQueryJSON('type:expense merchant:Amazon')?.hash).toEqual(1692688529)` (the pre-#83733 value) and drop the drift comment. - Round trip: `buildUserReadableQueryString(buildSearchQueryJSON('type:expense merchant:coffee'))` returns `type:expense merchant:coffee`. `getQueryWithUpdatedValues('merchant:coffee')` contains no `*`. - `merchant*:coffee` still parses as `contains` and comes back as `merchant:coffee`, with the same hash as `merchant:coffee`. - `merchant=coffee` still comes back as `merchant=coffee`, with a different hash from `merchant:coffee`. - Merchant filter form set to "Contains" builds `merchant:coffee`, and "Exactly matches" builds `merchant=coffee`. ### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional) - Special-casing merchant `contains` inside `buildFilterValuesString` and `buildMerchantFilterQuery`, as suggested above. It works, but it leaves the map saying contains is `*:`, so any future serializer that reads the map brings the bug back. It also needs the same fix in two places. - Fixing only `buildUserReadableQueryString` or the router. That leaves `*` in the URL and in the hashes, so the hash drift stays. Contributor details Your Expensify account email: zackthompson317@gmail.com Upwork Profile Link: https://www.upwork.com/freelancers/~010ec78449791d4046 Contributor details Expensify account email: sijo0218@gmail.com Upwork Profile Link: https://www.upwork.com/freelancers/~011091133bbb09cd1c ## Proposal ### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue. When searching for an expense using the merchant filter (e.g. `merchant:coffee`), reopening or re-submitting the search query causes an asterisk (`*`) to be automatically added to the colon, rewriting the query as `merchant*:coffee`. ### What is the root cause of that problem? Regression introduced in PR #83733 ("Add Contains / Equal to match type for the Merchant filter"): 1. In `src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts`, `operatorToCharMap[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.CONTAINS]` maps the `CONTAINS` operator to `*:` (line 64). 2. In `buildMerchantFilterQuery` (line 155): ```typescript operator = selectedMerchantOperator === CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO ? EXPLICIT_EQUAL_TO_OPERATOR : operatorToCharMap[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.CONTAINS]; ``` When the merchant operator is `CONTAINS` (the default), it serializes the operator using `operatorToCharMap[CONTAINS]` which produces `*:`, returning `merchant*:coffee`. 3. Similarly in `buildFilterValuesString` (lines 675–678): ```typescript const operatorChar = filterName === CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.MERCHANT && queryFilter.operator === CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO ? EXPLICIT_EQUAL_TO_OPERATOR : operatorToCharMap[queryFilter.operator]; ``` For `filterName === MERCHANT` and `operator === CONTAINS`, it falls back to `operatorToCharMap[CONTAINS]`, writing `*:` instead of `:`. 4. As a result, whenever a query containing `merchant:coffee` is rebuilt or parsed by the search router, it gets converted to `merchant*:coffee`. ### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem? 1. In `src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts:buildMerchantFilterQuery` (line 155): Use the canonical `:` operator for `CONTAINS` match on merchant rather than `*:`: ```typescript operator = selectedMerchantOperator === CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO ? EXPLICIT_EQUAL_TO_OPERATOR : operatorToCharMap[CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO]; ``` 2. In `src/libs/SearchQueryUtils.ts:buildFilterValuesString` (lines 675–678): Ensure `MERCHANT` with `CONTAINS` operator uses `:` instead of `*:`: ```typescript const operatorChar = filterName === CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_FILTER_KEYS.MERCHANT ? (queryFilter.operator === CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.EQUAL_TO ? EXPLICIT_EQUAL_TO_OPERATOR : :) : operatorToCharMap[queryFilter.operator]; ``` This preserves standard `merchant:value` query syntax while keeping `merchant=value` for explicit exact matches. ### What alternative solutions did you explore? ## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?
This is a regression from [Bump @react-navigation/bottom-tabs to 7.18.16 and @react-navigation/native to 7.3.16](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/103346), merged 2026-10-12.

When the panel opens, the app adds a `CUSTOM_HISTORY-SIDE_PANEL` marker to the end of the root navigator's `history`. That pushes one browser entry. [`useSyncSidePanelWithHistory`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/SidePanel/useSyncSidePanelWithHistory/index.ts#L58-L63) closes the panel when that marker stops being the last entry.

- **Before (7.1.x):** On `popstate`, `useLinking` called `resetRoot(record.state)`. That state has no marker, so the hook closed the panel.
- **Now (7.3+, currently 7.4.1):** `useLinking` has a new shortcut. When exactly one entry is popped (`isPoppingLastEntry`), it dispatches `CommonActions.goBack()` with no target and skips `resetRoot`. The deepest focused child navigator handles that `goBack`, not the root, so the root marker stays. The hook never fires, and the panel stays open.

<details>
<summary>Code references</summary>

- Marker added and removed: [`GetStateForActionHandlers.ts:781-787`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L781-L787)
- New branch in `node_modules/@react-navigation/native/lib/module/useLinking.js:307-319`. `isPoppingLastEntry` (lines 84-92) returns `true` because root `history` lengths differ only by the marker.
- Trailing string markers survive child state updates: [`addRootHistoryRouterExtension.ts:50-53`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/routerExtensions/addRootHistoryRouterExtension.ts#L50-L53)
- The Help button calls the normal `openSidePanel`, so the same hook applies: [`SidePanelButtonBase.tsx:37`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/SidePanel/SidePanelButton/SidePanelButtonBase.tsx#L37)
- The timing fits: the bump shipped in 9.5.12 (prod 2026-10-16) and is in the 9.5.13-3 build where this was reported.

</details>

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
Extend the existing patch [`@react-navigation+native+7.4.1+001+initial.patch`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/patches/react-navigation/@react-navigation+native+7.4.1+001+initial.patch). Skip the `goBack` shortcut when the entry being popped is one of the app's custom string history markers, meaning the last `history` item is a string rather than a route object. `useLinking` then falls back to `resetRoot(record.state, …)`, which matches the old behavior. That removes the marker, so the hook closes the panel. Document the change in [`patches/react-navigation/details.md`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/patches/react-navigation/details.md).

This should also fix other string markers that rely on browser Back, such as modals that use `shouldHandleNavigationBack` and the MFA navigator. I have not verified those.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Target `goBack` at the matched root navigator, and teach `RootStackRouter` to drop a trailing string marker on `GO_BACK`. This needs two changes and carries more risk.
- An app-only fix in the hook won't work, because the root router never receives the `GO_BACK`.

<details>
<summary>Confidence and testing</summary>

**Medium.** I traced the mechanism in code for both library versions. I have not reproduced it at runtime: the web test harness can't trigger browser Back. It did confirm the Help button opens the panel as a full-screen overlay at 390x844. Desktop Back at narrow or medium widths should fail the same way. On extra-large widths the panel is docked and is not synced with history by design.

[\[$250\] Gesture - Safari on iPhone flickers previous screen on swipe-back gesture](https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/75905) is possibly related (same gesture), but it describes a different symptom.

</details>

## Proposal

3. It then calls `dispatch(CommonActions.goBack())` with **no `target`**. So the `GO_BACK` is handled by a child navigator (for example the chat's split navigator), and the root `history` keeps the marker. The hook never sees a change.
4. Even if the root did receive a plain `GO_BACK`, our root router would get it wrong: `router.getStateForAction` would pop a route, and `getRehydratedState` re-appends trailing string sentinels ([addRootHistoryRouterExtension.ts:50-53](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/routerExtensions/addRootHistoryRouterExtension.ts#L50-L53)). 1. **Target the back action** in our existing patch `patches/react-navigation/@react-navigation+native+7.4.1+001+initial.patch` (`useLinking.js`, the `isPoppingLastEntry` branch):
```js
dispatch(
    {...CommonActions.goBack(), target: currentFocused.key},
    pending === 'replace' ? 'replace' : (pending ?? 0) - 1,
);
```
`currentFocused` is exactly the navigator whose history shrank, so this is correct for every case, not only string markers. For normal stack pops it's the same navigator the untargeted action reached before, so nothing changes there.     return {...state, history: asCustomHistory(state.history)?.slice(0, -1)};

- Skip the `isPoppingLastEntry` shortcut for string markers and fall back to `resetRoot(record.state)`. It works for the basic repro, but it discards state changed since the panel opened, as described above.

When the workspace's approval workflows are saved as rules (the new rules structure, used when the `multipleApprovers` beta is on), the App checks the approval limit at **submit** time instead of when the limited approver **approves**.

- Submit, from B, amount < $100 → forward to C
- Submit, from B, amount ≥ $100 → forward to A ← B's $150 report matches this rule and skips C
- Approve, to C or A → approve

The App then applies this rule when B submits. [`getSubmitToEmail`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/PolicyUtils/approvals.ts#L334-L363) returns A, and `submitReport` sends A as `managerAccountID`.

1. In `buildApprovalWorkflowRules`, move the amount split from the rule that leads *into* C onto C's own **approve** rule:
   - Submit, from B → forward to C
   - Approve, to C, amount over the limit → forward to A

3. Update the parsers that read the rules back (`resolvePositionHolders` and `buildApproverChainFromRules`) so the workflow page still shows "C, limit $100, over-limit A".

Workspaces that already saved limits with the old rules keep the wrong routing until an admin saves the workflow again, or until those rules are migrated.

Keep the "instead of" routing and change the UI copy to match it. I don't recommend this. It contradicts the expected result in this issue and how approval limits worked before.

A report equal to the limit ($100) is within the approver's authority and should not trigger the over-limit forwarder. The comparison should strictly be `>` (`GREATER_THAN`).

3. **Conceptual Misalignment (Submit vs. Approve):**
   Approval limits do not dictate submission routing; they dictate approval authority. All submissions must route to the primary approver first. The over-limit forwarder is only evaluated when the primary approver executes an `APPROVE` action.

---

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In `src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts`:

1. **Do not branch on amount for Position 0 Submit Triggers:**
   In `buildRulesIntoPosition`, the rules routing into position 0 (`triggers: buildSubmitTriggers()`) must unconditionally forward to `holders.underLimitEmail` (the primary approver):
   ```ts
   if (isFirstPosition) {
       rulesIntoPosition.push({triggers, filters: source, actions: buildForwardActions(holders.underLimitEmail)});
       return rulesIntoPosition;
   }
   ```

2. **Branch on Amount for the Position's `APPROVE` Triggers:**
   When an approver with an approval limit approves the report:
   - If `amount > limit`: forward to `holders.overLimitEmail`.
   - If `amount <= limit`: forward to the next approver in the chain, or finalize approval (`buildApproveActions()`) if this is the final position.
   - Use `CONST.SEARCH.SYNTAX_OPERATORS.GREATER_THAN` strictly for the over-limit condition.

3. **Update Parsers (`resolvePositionHolders` & `buildApproverChainFromRules`):**
   Ensure `resolvePositionHolders` reads the amount split from the `APPROVE` rules when reconstructing the workflow chain, so the Workflows UI continues to display `Approver: User C, Approval Limit: $100, Over-limit Approver: User A` accurately.

4. **Update Existing Unit Tests & Add Regression Coverage:**
   Update existing fixtures in `tests/unit/WorkflowUtilsTest.ts` to reflect the updated rule structure.

---

### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests?

In `tests/unit/WorkflowUtilsTest.ts`:
1. **Submit Routing with Over-Limit Amount:**
   - Configure a workflow: Submitter User B, Approver User C (limit: $100, over-limit approver: User A).
   - Verify that generating rules produces a `SUBMIT` rule from User B that forwards to User C regardless of whether the report amount is $50, $100, or $150.
2. **Approve Routing at Limit Boundaries:**
   - Verify that an `APPROVE` action by User C with amount `$100` (`<= limit`) finalizes the report / does not forward to User A.
   - Verify that an `APPROVE` action by User C with amount `$150` (`> limit`) forwards to User A.
3. **Round-Trip Conversion:**
   - Verify that `convertApprovalWorkflowRulesToWorkflows` reconstructs the approver chain with `approvalLimit` and `overLimitForwardsTo` intact.

---

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

1. **Retaining "instead of" routing and updating UI copy:**
   - *Rejected:* Modifying the UI copy to say "Over-limit reports bypass User C and go directly to User A" contradicts Expensify's long-standing tiered approval workflow model where primary approvers review first before escalating.
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
In a Control workspace with rules-based approval workflows (`multipleApprovers` beta), submitting an expense report exceeding an approver's approval limit submits the report directly to the over-limit approver instead of routing to the primary approver first.

---

### What is the root cause of that problem?

In [`src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts:896-936`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts#L896-L936), `buildApprovalWorkflowRules` -> `buildRulesIntoPosition` constructs the amount threshold on the rules routing *into* each position.

1. For position 0 (the first approver), `triggers` are `buildSubmitTriggers()`.
2. When the primary approver has an approval limit and an over-limit approver, it generates two `ReportSubmit`-triggered rules:
   - `ReportSubmit`, submitter in member list, `amount < limit` $\to$ `ForwardTo: primaryApprover`
   - `ReportSubmit`, submitter in member list, `amount >= limit` $\to$ `ForwardTo: overLimitApprover`
3. When User B submits a $\$150$ report, [`getSubmitToEmail`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/PolicyUtils/approvals.ts#L334-L363) matches the second submit rule via [`getForwardsToFromRules`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/PolicyUtils/approvals.ts#L277-L302), submitting the report directly to the over-limit approver (User A) and completely bypassing primary approver User C.
4. Additionally, using `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO` (`>=`) instead of `GREATER_THAN` (`>`) causes reports equal to the threshold to also bypass the primary approver, conflicting with existing policy behavior ([`approvals.ts:430`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/PolicyUtils/approvals.ts#L430)).
5. In reverse, [`buildApproverChainFromRules`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts#L1422-L1474) reads limits from the incoming transition rather than from the approver's own `ReportApprove` rules.

---

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. **In [`src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts#L874-L957) (`buildApprovalWorkflowRules`)**:
   - The `ReportSubmit` rule should always forward to the first approver without any amount conditions.
   - Move the amount split to the primary approver's own `ReportApprove` triggers:
     - When the primary approver approves and `amount > limit` (`GREATER_THAN`), forward to `overLimitForwardsTo`.
     - When the primary approver approves and `amount <= limit` (`LOWER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO`), forward to the next approver in the chain (or finalize with `ApproveReport` if it is the last position).
     - When the `overLimitForwardsTo` approver approves, forward to the next approver in the chain (or finalize with `ApproveReport` if it is the last position). This ensures the over-limit approver can finalize or advance the report once approved.

2. **In [`src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/WorkflowUtils.ts#L1422-L1474) (`buildApproverChainFromRules`)**:
   - Update `buildApproverChainFromRules` to obtain the initial approver from submission and resolve each approver's `approvalLimit`, `overLimitForwardsTo`, and `forwardsTo` from their own `ReportApprove` rules (retaining fallback to `firstApproverHolders` for backward compatibility with previously saved workflows).

3. **In [`tests/unit/WorkflowUtilsTest.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/tests/unit/WorkflowUtilsTest.ts#L2365-L2465)**:
   - Update the existing unit tests to reflect that submission routes to the first approver and the over-limit split triggers upon approval.
   - Add a regression test verifying that User B's $\$150$ submission routes to primary approver User C and forwards to User A on approval.

---

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keep the "instead of" submit-time routing and update UI copy. Rejected: this contradicts the core Expensify workflow philosophy (an approval limit specifies when an additional approval step is required after primary review, not a replacement on submission) and breaks existing expectation contracts.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
Arrow navigation ("1 of 2") remains visible in a report header and navigates to an "It's not here" screen even when only one valid expense remains after deleting split expenses.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
When an expense is split into child expenses, its original container transaction is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` (`-2`) in `src/libs/actions/IOU/SplitTransactionUpdate.ts` (lines 1706-1715).

In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts` (line 43), `validTransactionIDsSelector` only filters out expenses that are pending delete or deleted:
`return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);`
Because the original container transaction is neither marked deleted nor pending delete, it remains in `validTransactionIDs`. The container transaction never leaves.

When both created split expenses are deleted, only the single remaining non-split expense exists on the report. However, `useCarouselTransactionIDs` continues returning both the remaining expense and the container transaction (length of 2). Because of this, `MoneyReportHeader.tsx` (line 108) evaluates `activeTransactionIDs.length > 1` as true, showing the "1 of 2" arrow navigation.

Clicking the navigation arrow invokes `navigateToSibling` in `MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx`. In `canResolveSibling` (lines 322-344) and `resolveSiblingReportID` (lines 258-312), the logic only guards against `CONST.REPORT.UNREPORTED_REPORT_ID` (`0`), not `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` (`-2`). The app attempts to navigate to target report ID `-2`. Because report `-2` does not exist, the user lands on the "It's not here" page.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`, update `validTransactionIDsSelector` to filter out split container transactions:
`return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction) && !isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction);`
Import `isSplitContainerTransaction` from `@libs/TransactionUtils`. This reactively drops the split container from the carousel as soon as `reportID` updates to `-2`.

2. In `src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx`:
   - In `canResolveSibling` (line 327), add an early return of `false` if `siblingTransaction?.reportID === CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. This check must sit right at the start of the function, before checking descriptors or `siblingParentReportAction?.childReportID`, ensuring a split container never resolves as an openable sibling.
   - In `resolveSiblingReportID` (line 265), add an early return of `undefined` if `siblingTransaction?.reportID === CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`.

3. Add unit test coverage in `tests/unit/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDsTest.ts` verifying that `useCarouselTransactionIDs` excludes transactions assigned to `SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. In `tests/unit/components/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigationTest.tsx`, verify that `canResolveSibling` and `resolveSiblingReportID` reject siblings with `reportID === SPLIT_REPORT_ID` even when a descriptor or report action exists.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
Earlier proposals by @MelvinBot and @camesenin only proposed adding `!isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction)` to `useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts` and placing a guard at the end of `canResolveSibling`.

Their fatal flaw is that adding the check only at line 343 in `canResolveSibling` misses the earlier returns for descriptors and child report actions on lines 330-333. If an action or descriptor exists for the sibling, `canResolveSibling` returns true before line 343, keeping the arrow clickable. Placing the guard at the top of both `canResolveSibling` and `resolveSiblingReportID` guarantees that report `-2` is rejected before any descriptor or action resolution runs.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
After splitting an expense and then deleting both splits, the report is left with one expense, but the header still shows "1 of 2" arrows, and the arrow opens the "It's not here" page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The prev/next carousel is a global seed (`TRANSACTION_THREAD_NAVIGATION_TRANSACTION_IDS`) written when an expense row is opened, here `[A, B]` with source `reportRow:<reportID>`. The app's contract is that **whoever moves an expense off a report prunes it from that report's carousel**. `changeTransactionsReport` does this for every move via `removeMovedTransactionsFromCarousel` → `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport` (added in #103998):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/actions/Transaction.ts#L2144-L2152

Splitting is a move that skips that contract. `updateSplitTransactions` moves the original expense B to the hidden split report `-2` with a direct Onyx `SET`, and never touches the carousel:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/actions/IOU/SplitTransactionUpdate.ts#L1706-L1715

So the seed keeps `[A, B]` even though B is no longer on the report. Deleting the two splits doesn't change it (they were never in the seed). Once A is the only expense, `MoneyReportHeader` anchors on it, sees two IDs, and shows "1 of 2". The arrow then resolves B to report `-2`.

The earlier proposals filter B out inside `useCarouselTransactionIDs` (line 43). That hides the header arrows, but the stale seed is still in Onyx and in the module state, and **not every consumer goes through that hook**. `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` reads the raw key and treats any seed longer than 1 as "the user is stepping through expenses":

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/pages/inbox/OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler.tsx#L30-L32
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/pages/inbox/OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler.tsx#L83-L91

With the stale `[A, B]`, that check stays `true` for A's thread even though A is now the only expense on its report, so the normal one-transaction redirect to the parent report is suppressed. A hook-only filter fixes the arrows but leaves this second symptom of the same stale seed.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. **Fix it where the move happens.** In `updateSplitTransactions`, in the non-reverse branch right after `writeSplit(...)` (`SplitTransactionUpdate.ts` ~L2158-L2174), prune the original from its old report's carousel using the existing helper, the same way `changeTransactionsReport` does:
```ts
// Splitting moves the original to SPLIT_REPORT_ID, so it must leave the carousel seeded from its old report,
// just like a regular move (see removeMovedTransactionsFromCarousel).
if (isCreationOfSplits && originalTransaction?.reportID && originalTransaction.reportID !== CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID) {
    removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport([originalTransactionID], originalTransaction.reportID);
}
```
`removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport` already only acts when the carousel is owned by that report (`report:`/`reportRow:`/`reportPreview:` sources), leaves search carousels alone, and clears the carousel when fewer than 2 IDs remain. So it can't break the arrows on Search. If the user is in the split-expenses flow, the call can go inside the existing `TransitionTracker.runAfterTransitions` callback next to `removeDraftSplitTransaction` so it doesn't re-render mid-transition.

2. **Defense in depth (optional, agreeing with earlier proposals):** also return `false` for `isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction)` in `validTransactionIDsSelector`, and have `canResolveSibling` reject `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` the same way it rejects `UNREPORTED_REPORT_ID` (L343). This covers a seed that was restored from somewhere else, but on its own it doesn't fix the raw-key consumer above.

3. **Tests:**
   - In `tests/unit/libs/actions/TransactionThreadNavigationTest.ts`-style setup, seed `[A, B]` with source `reportRow:R`, call `updateSplitTransactions` creating splits from B, and assert the carousel no longer contains B (and is cleared, since only A remains).
   - Assert a carousel seeded from `search:<hash>` is left untouched by the split.
   - Assert `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` redirects A's thread to the parent report after the splits are deleted.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Filtering only in `useCarouselTransactionIDs` (earlier proposals): fixes the header, but leaves the stale seed for `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` and any future raw-key reader, and breaks the "writer prunes on move" pattern from #103998.
- Re-seeding from `useMoneyRequestReportActiveTransactionIDs` outside Search: rejected, because that hook is deliberately Search-only to avoid clobbering carousels owned by other screens.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

After splitting an expense and deleting both splits, the report is left with a single expense, but the report header still renders the "1 of 2" prev/next arrows, and tapping an arrow opens the "It’s not here" page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The prev/next carousel is seeded when an expense row is opened, stored under ONYXKEYS.TRANSACTION_THREAD_NAVIGATION_TRANSACTION_IDS. The codebase has an established contract: whoever moves an expense off a report prunes it from that report's carousel, implemented by removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport and enforced for every move through changeTransactionsReport (added in PR #103998).

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Fix it where the move happens, not in the consumers:

1. Inviting a new member with a non-existing account to an expense thread or room leaves the member missing from the members list until the page is refreshed.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

ewAccountIDs).
2. optimisticData adds this temporary account ID to 
eport.participants and creates temporary personal details via PersonalDetailsUtils.getPersonalDetailsOnyxDataForOptimisticUsers.
3. However, successData unconditionally cleans up the optimistic data:
   - 
ewParticipantAccountCleanUp sets 
eport.participants[newAccountID] = null.

ewPersonalDetailsOnyxData.finallyData purges the temporary personal details.
4. For expense threads and chat rooms, the backend InviteToRoom command returns the new real participant ID in the response, but omits the matching personalDetailsList entry.

Once the public profile resolves, Onyx updates personalDetailsList, automatically restoring the member row and count in DynamicRoomMembersPage.

eport_<reportID>.participants[accountID].

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

User A creates two expenses for User B. User B opens one of the expenses, taps the header, opens Members, and invites a member whose email has no existing Expensify account. The invited member is not shown in the members list after the invite, and the member count stays unchanged. The invited member only appears after the page is refreshed.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

For a login with no existing account, `DynamicRoomInvitePage` passes an optimistic accountID, generated by hashing the login in `generateAccountID`, to `inviteToRoom`. In `buildInviteToRoomOnyxData` in `src/libs/actions/Report/index.ts`, that optimistic ID is added to `report.participants` and an optimistic personal detail is created for it through `getPersonalDetailsOnyxDataForOptimisticUsers` in `PersonalDetailsUtils`. The success data for the same request then unconditionally cleans both up: it sets `participants[optimisticID]` to null and deletes the optimistic personal detail. That cleanup assumes the `InviteToRoom` response has already added the participant and the personal detail under the real accountID that the server creates for the new login.

For an expense thread, that response does not add the thread participant or the personal detail for the newly created account, so after the success cleanup nothing for the invited member is left in Onyx. The list could not show the member even if a participant entry remained, because `getParticipantsList` in `src/libs/ReportUtils.ts`, used by `DynamicRoomMembersPage`, filters out any participant who has no personal detail, and `DynamicRoomMembersPage` builds its rows only from participants with personal details.

Nothing then reloads the members. `DynamicRoomMembersPage` calls `openRoomMembersPage(reportID)` only once, in its mount effect, and the invite page navigates back to that already mounted page. A refresh remounts the page, runs `OpenRoomMembersPage`, and that read returns the real participant and personal detail, which is why the invited member appears only after a refresh. Inviting a login that already has an account is not affected, because no optimistic account is created or cleaned up for it.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In `inviteToRoom` in `src/libs/actions/Report/index.ts`, when the invite includes new accounts, meaning `newAccountIDs` is not empty, queue an `openRoomMembersPage(report.reportID)` read for the same report right after the `InviteToRoom` write. Requests run in order, so the read runs after the invite has been processed and returns the participant and the `personalDetailsList` entry the server created under the real accountID. Merging that read into Onyx replaces the cleaned up optimistic entries with the real ones.

Keep the existing optimistic data and success cleanup in `buildInviteToRoomOnyxData` unchanged, and do not trigger the extra read when every invited login already has an account, since those invites already update correctly from the write response. This also covers `DynamicReportParticipantsInvitePage`, which reaches the same code through `inviteToGroupChat`.

Result: after inviting a member with a non existing account to an expense thread, returning to Members shows the invited member right away, with the correct member count, and no refresh is needed. Invites of existing accounts, and the members list itself, behave as before.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keeping the optimistic participant and the optimistic personal detail in the success data, instead of cleaning them up. I did not choose this because the optimistic accountID is a hash of the login, not the real accountID, so the row would point at the wrong account, member details and removal would act on the wrong ID, and a duplicate row would appear once the real personal detail is loaded later.

Refetching members in `DynamicRoomMembersPage` every time the page regains focus. This would fix the list when the user returns to it, but the report details member count would still be wrong until the members page is reopened, and every return to the page would pay for a read that is only needed after an invite of a new account.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The default column logic shows From only when at least one row has an actor other than you ([`SearchUIUtils.ts:6887-6892`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/3b2393bcd9d666cbef6fabbf83e11134246005aa/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L6887-L6892)). This rule is intentional. It came from [Auto show/hide columns depending on available data](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/68561), but it does not consider an explicit `from:` filter.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
Always show From when the query has a `from:` filter. This follows the existing pattern for the Violations column (`queryHasViolationFilter`).

1. In `SearchQueryUtils.ts`, add `queryHasFromFilter(queryJSON)`. It returns true when `flatFilters` has a `from` key.
2. Add a `shouldShowFromColumn` parameter to `getColumnsToShow`. Show From when it is true or when the existing other-actor check passes.
3. Pass `queryHasFromFilter(queryJSON)` from `useSearchColumnsToShow`. For consistency, also pass it from `useSearchOverlay`, `SortByPopup`, and `useSearchBulkActions`.
4. Add a unit test: all rows belong to the current user, From is hidden by default and shown with a `from:` filter.
